title: Minimum Cost to Connect Two Groups of Points
statement:
There are two groups of points: a left group with `size1` points and a right group with `size2` points, where `size1 >= size2`. The matrix `cost` has `size1` rows and `size2` columns, and `cost[i][j]` is the price of drawing an edge between left point `i` and right point `j`.

Choose a set of edges so that every point on both sides touches at least one chosen edge. A point may touch any number of edges, and each chosen edge is paid for once. Return the smallest possible total price.
notes:
## Intuition

Trying every set of edges is exponential in `size1 * size2`, far too many. Two facts make the search small. First, each left point needs only one edge of "its own". Second, any right point that no left point picked can simply be joined by its cheapest edge, `cheapest[j]`, since costs are never negative and nothing else depends on that edge. So we only need to decide, row by row, which single right point each left point takes, while remembering which right points are already touched. With at most 12 right points, that memory fits in a bitmask.

## Approach

1. For each column `j`, compute `cheapest[j]`, the smallest cost in that column.
2. `dp[mask]` is the least cost after handling some rows, where `mask` is the set of right points those rows touched. Start with `dp[0] = 0`.
3. For each row `i`, build `next`: from every reachable `mask`, let row `i` take any column `j`, landing on `mask | (1 << j)` with cost `dp[mask] + cost[i][j]`.
4. After all rows, for each `mask` add `cheapest[j]` for every column missing from it, and keep the smallest `total` as `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

`cost = [[15, 96], [36, 2]]`, so `cheapest = [15, 2]`. Row 0 gives `dp[01] = 15` and `dp[10] = 96`. Row 1 gives `dp[01] = 51`, `dp[10] = 98` and `dp[11] = min(15 + 2, 96 + 36) = 17`. Finishing: mask `01` costs `51 + 2 = 53`, mask `10` costs `98 + 15 = 113`, mask `11` costs `17`. The answer is `17`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(size1 · 2^size2 · size2): each row tries every column from every mask.
- Space: O(2^size2) for the two rows of `dp`.

## Pitfalls

- Put the bitmask over the smaller group (columns); a mask over 12 rows works too but the problem guarantees columns are fewer.
- Do not stop at `dp[full]`: leaving some right points for the final `cheapest` pass is often cheaper.
- Every row must take exactly one column, so `next` starts at `Infinity` and the old `dp` is never carried over unchanged.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `rows`, `cols` | sizes of the left and right groups |
| `full` | number of masks, `2^cols` |
| `cheapest[j]` | cheapest edge into right point `j` |
| `dp[mask]` | least cost so far with right points `mask` touched |
| `next` | the `dp` row after adding row `i` |
| `joined` | the mask after row `i` takes column `j` |
| `total`, `best` | cost of finishing one mask, and the least of them |

narration.4: There are 2^cols possible sets of touched right points, one per bitmask.
narration.5: cheapest[j] will hold the lowest cost of any edge into right point j.
narration.8: Keep the smaller of the current best and this row's cost for column j.
narration.12: dp[mask] is the least cost so far for touching exactly the right points in mask; all start unreachable.
narration.13: Before any row is handled, nothing is touched and nothing is paid.
narration.14: Handle the left points one row at a time.
narration.15: next will hold the costs after row i has picked its edge.
narration.17: Skip masks that no earlier choice can reach.
narration.19: Row i takes column j, so j joins the touched set.
narration.20: Keep the cheaper way of reaching the joined mask.
narration.23: The new row of costs replaces the old one.
narration.27: Every left point is now connected; try each final set of touched right points.
narration.30: A right point no row picked is joined by its cheapest edge.
narration.32: Keep the cheapest way of finishing.
narration.34: Return the least total cost that connects both groups.
